sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Perth Amboy?
sections.html:
Perth Amboy has its own sale rule: a Certificate of Code Compliance must be in hand before a house is transferred, whether the buyer pays cash or finances. That single step shapes timing, repairs and who takes on what, so it deserves attention before a listing goes live.

The city sits on Raritan Bay and the Arthur Kill in northeastern Middlesex County, with 4.66 square miles of land and another 1.27 of water. The Census Bureau estimated 56,739 residents on July 1, 2025, packed at 11,891 people per square mile in the 2020 count, which makes it one of the densest places in the state. Buyers here often look at two-, three- and four-family buildings as well as single-family homes.

Settlement dates to 1683, when Scottish colonists arrived, and the city served as capital of East Jersey from 1686. Its royal charter dates to August 4, 1718, and City Hall, first built as a county courthouse in 1714, is described as the oldest city hall in continuous use in the country. Victorian houses climb the hills above the waterfront, and a clay layer hundreds of feet thick under the city fed a terra cotta industry in the late 1800s.

sections.h2: What does the Perth Amboy Certificate of Code Compliance require?
sections.html:
Chapter 181 of the city code bars any transfer, conveyance or sale of a residential, commercial or industrial building until the Department of Code Enforcement issues the certificate. The inspection checks zoning, the fire safety code and substantial conformity with the property maintenance code.

The code gives sellers several ways to keep a closing on schedule:

  • A conditional certificate can run 45 days, and the Director may grant a second 45 days on request.
  • A buyer who says in writing that the purchase is as-is can receive a temporary, nonrenewable certificate good for up to six months from transfer, unless a life-safety hazard exists.
  • A certificate may issue even if the building does not match every code, provided it is in substantial compliance and safe, sound and sturdy.
  • A denial can be appealed in writing within 10 days to a three-member Certificate of Code Compliance Appeals Board.

Some transfers are exempt, including those between immediate family members, transfers through probate, sales of a building inspected or certified within the previous six months, and purchases made to demolish the building. Violations carry a fine up to $1,000, jail up to 90 days, or both, with each day counted separately. The code also lists a $25 per unit residential reinspection fee and exempts holders of a senior citizen property tax exemption from the fees. Ask Code Enforcement for current inspection charges, because the fee table printed in the code is a multi-year schedule that began in 2012.

sections.h2: How many Perth Amboy homes are rentals, and why does that matter?
sections.html:
Most of them. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied share at 35.4 percent for 2020 to 2024, so renters occupy the majority of homes. Median gross rent is $1,688 and median household income is $61,977.

A buyer of a tenant-occupied building steps into the city's rent control ordinance, Chapter 353, which a Rent Leveling Board enforces. Since November 1, 2022, increases are capped at 3 percent where water is included in rent and 2.5 percent where it is not. Periodic tenants on terms shorter than a year cannot be charged an increase until the tenancy passes twelve months. Anyone pricing a sale on rent growth should work from those caps.

The same Census survey reports that 50.7 percent of residents were born outside the United States, that 79.5 percent of people five and older speak a language other than English at home, and that 83.6 percent identify as Hispanic or Latino. Sale documents, disclosures and tenant notices work better when offered in English and Spanish. The city publishes its rent control information in both.

sections.h2: Do historic district rules affect a Perth Amboy sale?
sections.html:
They can, if the building stands in or beside a historic district. The Historic Preservation Commission, formed in 1993, reviews proposed changes to designated sites and structures and new construction within or next to districts, under Chapter 258 of the city code.

The historic waterfront neighborhood holds much of the old building stock, including the Proprietary House built in 1764 as a royal governor's residence, and Market Square across from City Hall. A buyer planning exterior changes in that area should expect commission review, so mention it up front when you market the house.

sections.h2: How do the roads and transit around Perth Amboy affect buyers?
sections.html:
Perth Amboy puts buyers within reach of New York and central Jersey. The Outerbridge Crossing, opened June 29, 1928, links the city to Staten Island, and the Victory Bridge carries Route 35 across the Raritan River to Sayreville. Route 440, Route 184, County Route 501 and County Route 616 also serve the city.

NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line stops at Perth Amboy station, with service to Newark Penn Station, Hoboken, Secaucus Junction and New York Penn Station. Bus 116 runs to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. The Census Bureau lists a mean commute of 23.5 minutes, among the shorter ones in the county.

Perth Amboy Public Schools, a former Abbott district, ran 12 schools and about 10,800 students in 2020 to 2021. The Middlesex County Magnet Schools also operate a campus in the city, and Catholic schools in the Diocese of Metuchen serve grades pre-K to 8.

sections.h2: How are the deed and the taxes handled for a Perth Amboy sale?
sections.html:
The city assessor keeps records on more than 9,500 properties and reviews every transfer. Ask the Tax Collection office for a tax search and payoff figure before the closing date, and check that the assessor has your correct mailing address.

The deed is recorded with the Middlesex County Clerk, Registry Division, on the fourth floor of the County Administration Building at 75 Bayard Street in New Brunswick, open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:10 p.m., with a 4 p.m. arrival cutoff. A paper filing without the required cover sheet draws a $20 indexing charge. Title companies can file electronically around the clock through the New Jersey County Recording portal.

If the house sits in an estate, the executor signs the seller's Gross Income Tax form on the estate's behalf, and the city's code exempts probate transfers from the compliance certificate. Heirs who sell after taking title sign for themselves, using the form that matches their own residency.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer help a Perth Amboy seller?
sections.html:
A cash offer helps when the building would fail the code inspection, carries tenants a seller no longer wants to manage, or must close before a conditional certificate runs out. In each case the as-is certificate route can let the buyer take the repairs after closing.

Ask any buyer whether the offer assumes the temporary certificate, who pays for inspections, and how existing leases and security deposits will be handled. Compare offers by net proceeds, not by the top-line price.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell a house in Perth Amboy?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 181 of the city code requires a Certificate of Code Compliance before a residential or commercial building is transferred, for cash and financed sales alike.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Perth Amboy house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. If the buyer states in writing that the purchase is as-is, the city can issue a temporary, nonrenewable certificate for up to six months, unless a life-safety condition exists.

faqs.q: Are probate and family transfers exempt in Perth Amboy?
faqs.a: Yes. The code exempts transfers between immediate family members and transfers made through probate proceedings from the certificate requirement.

faqs.q: How much can rent rise in a Perth Amboy rental I am selling?
faqs.a: Up to 3 percent a year where water is included and 2.5 percent where it is not, under the rent control cap in force since November 1, 2022.

faqs.q: Where is a Perth Amboy deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Middlesex County Clerk's Registry Division at 75 Bayard Street in New Brunswick, or electronically through the county's e-recording portal for title companies and attorneys.
